mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain depressed while RESIDENTIAL stays elevated, discretionary outings are constrained and retail-and-recreation demand stays soft. Over the next four weeks this should keep RETAIL_REC below the prior four-week average.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain near their current levels yet RETAIL_REC rises above its last-four-week mean over the next 28 days, this mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A further drop in TRANSIT of more than 2 points week-on-week signals weaker citywide circulation, which should translate into lower retail visits within one to two weeks. If transit does not breach that threshold, the retail effect should not appear.
failure_condition: If TRANSIT falls by more than 2 points week-on-week and RETAIL_REC does not decline within the following 14 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM both move up together, residents are reallocating trips toward local utility and outdoor activities rather than shopping districts. That substitution should keep RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM both rise for two consecutive weeks but RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days, the interaction mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In a tightening-restrictions regime, persistent TRANSIT weakness combined with below-baseline WORKPLACES implies continued suppression of discretionary travel. Under that regime, retail-and-recreation mobility should stay below the recent four-week mean over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If restrictions tighten but RETAIL_REC does not stay below its last-four-week average over the next 28 days, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS after a trough often precedes broader leisure activity, and that spillover lifts retail visits with about a one-week lag. Because PARKS is still well below its recent minimum-to-baseline swing, a continued recovery should push RETAIL_REC up.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above its prior week's level after a two-week decline
failure_condition: If PARKS rises after a two-week decline and RETAIL_REC does not increase within 7 days, the seasonal rebound hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL remains above baseline while WORKPLACES stays weak, more trips are likely to be local and time-shifted toward neighborhood shopping. That pattern should modestly lift RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL stays above baseline and WORKPLACES remains depressed yet RETAIL_REC falls over the next 14 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM is flat to slightly down while TRANSIT is also weak, households are not substituting daily errands into city-center trips. That should keep RETAIL_REC lower than the previous four-week average over a four-week horizon.
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM drops below its four-week mean and RETAIL_REC still rises over the next 28 days, the mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: A short-run improvement in WORKPLACES of at least 3 points from one week to the next signals loosening attendance constraints, which should feed through to more shopping trips in the following week. If workplace mobility does not improve, retail mobility should not accelerate.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by at least 3 points week-on-week
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES rises by at least 3 points week-on-week and RETAIL_REC does not increase within 7 days, the hypothesis is rejected.
